utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am asking this for a very simple reason, that is, that it wasn't clear during the Milosevic trial, it wasn't clear to me and I wanted to clarify it with the witness, because as she described her life at the time, I had understood that she was living there, which was clashing with what I knew from other sources that at the time she was already living somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That may very well be true and correct, Mr. Lukic, and you do need to make those clarifications. But in doing so, don't confuse us further, you know, because you're now attributing to the Prosecution statements that I don't see anywhere, and in the process now I'm getting lost, because I'm trying to find out in my mind where was it alleged that it was in her residence when she got injured. And sitting here I'm trying to recollect from my reading of her statement, my remembrance is that she moved from her residence to a place somewhere to go and collect wood, and it was there that she was injured. Now, how you come to that conclusion, I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to find it in the Milosevic transcript. Just a moment, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means, sir. And I hope you do appreciate the importance, therefore, of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- giving references when you put previous statements to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Madam, you don't recall or you do recall whether at that time, on the day when the incident occurred, you were there.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was there. Where was I? I was there. I know that. That's where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "you were there," I don't understand what you mean? Where? Where, Mr. Lukic? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the location where she was hit in front of the shed where she was collecting wood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. And I think if you go to paragraph 3 of her statement of 12th of March, you will see there where she says she was when she got hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you will see that that wasn't her current residence, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. That's how I understand the statement. In the transcript there was mention of the fact -- in cross-examination she was asked where she was residing at the time she was injured, and I wanted to see whether it was necessary to refer back to the statement made to the police, because there it's stated precisely. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were asked on page 1598 in the Milosevic case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you give us the lines, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked by Judge Mindua, line 10: [In English] "The noise that you heard and that you heard also that day when you were hit, were they coming from the same direction or from various directions?" [Interpretation] Your answer was?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: From Spicaste, that was the closest part. That's where it came from. We heard the whiz of the bullet, and then it hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read to you what you said then. [In English] "I cannot tell you that. I don't know. I don't know. I cannot say. There was shooting, and you'd be hiding in the house most of the time. You know, you just hear shooting, and you run away to seek shelter."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: My apologies again, but before the witness answers, can I -- in order to avoid any misunderstanding between my learned friend and the witness, can I suggest that it's made clear that the answer quoted by the witness, which I quote "I cannot tell you that, I don't know," and so on, refers to the question asked by His Honour Judge Mindua about not the shot that hit the witness but other shooting going on that day, which can be inferred by the very same question by Judge Mindua, so that we avoid that the witness might answer with a wrong understanding of the question. I don't know if I made myself clear but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not to me. I don't know whether your learned friend understood you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask the witness a very precise question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were hit. After that you say you heard 20 or 30 more shots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: The bullets were raining down, "pu, pu, pu, pu, pu."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you: This shooting that was heard, how many bullets were there, according to you? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: How could I remember when they were shooting and I was hit by a bullet and then I thought only of myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there 20, 30, or more bullets?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: What do I know? It was just a shower of bullets. How could I count them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you: Do you know what a burst of fire is --

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- a burst from an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those are small bullets like infantry, and all of a sudden they just --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did it sound to you like automatic fire?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember every detail. What do I know? I just know that we were afraid, and we had to flee and run for shelter every day. And then I thought, Well, they won't fire now. I went to collect some wood, and when I least expected it, they were constantly shooting. They were always shooting, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't have to reply at such length. I simply asked you whether the fire you heard afterwards sounded like automatic fire or like individual shots. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I don't remember that. I can't tell you that. I only know that there was shooting, but I can't remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But before that you didn't hear a single shot fired that day?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was never a day without any shooting at all. There was never such a day, nor could there be such a day, or hour or minute, without something happening. But, you know, it was long away, and then it wouldn't be afraid, and if it was close by, then you'd be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell me precisely whether you remember on that day, before you were hit, when you went to that place where you were collecting firewood, did you hear shooting?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement to the OTP, you said, referring to Spicaste Stijena, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's in paragraph 3, Your Honours, of the first statement, Exhibit 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The snipers were constantly shooting from that position."

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "From there, there was constant sniper fire. Those positions were held by the Chetniks." In paragraph 4 you say: "I was perhaps a kilometre away from the sniper position, but the sniper could clearly see I was a civilian and a woman."

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, he could have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you how you know that.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, because it's nearby and because they have equipment which enables them to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were aware that a sniper can make such distinctions at the distance of a thousand metres, that they could tell who was a civilian?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: How would I know? I'd never seen a war before. I'd never been in a war before that. How would I know such things?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't see where the shot that hit you came from. You just felt pain in your knee.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I felt something like a large stone hit me. He fired until he hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you just answer my question, please. You did not see from where the bullet that hit you came. That's what I'm asking you. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: But Spicaste was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You sustained a slight physical injury on that day and were released home on the same day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were given a medical report?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: They told us that on the next day I should come again for my dressing to be changed on the wound, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, did they give you a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you get a document from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did get a letter of discharge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you give it to the police or the OTP? I apologise for asking, if you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. How could I remember that so many years later? There are too many questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking this, Your Honours, because in the Dragomir Milosevic judgement, in paragraph 357 and footnote 1269, I found mention of a medical report under seal. But I'll see that with the OTP later on. I never had a chance to see this medical report, and there were certain discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were hit with only one bullet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: One clarification. The document my learned friend is referring to is 65 ter 5 -- 4522. It's a medical report tendered under seal in the Dragomir Milosevic case. It was disclosed as part of the additional exhibits to this witness but it wasn't tendered to date. But it was disclosed to the Defence. And actually, it was disclosed on 16 March 2007 and again on 16 November 2007, so the Defence had possession of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata, when you say "it was disclosed as part of additional exhibits to this witness but it wasn't tendered to date," I'm not quite sure I understand. Disclosed to the witness or disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: It was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's a response there, Mr. Lukic. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. When I was looking at the documentation -- well, now it's been clarified, so I will clarify this with other witnesses who will be testifying about the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I'll just put a few more brief questions to you, madam. You said in your statements that the bullet came from the left, from the direction of Spicaste Stijena; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's what you said when you testified in the Dragomir Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now ask my learned friends from the OTP if they can play for us a video which is now in evidence, and it's number 114. It's the 42nd minute, 16 seconds, 42:16 is the time, and it's the reconstruction of the event you will recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll look at that, and then I'll ask you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "MR. HOGAN: Witness, at this point I would like you to please to point to the location on your body where the bullet hit you on the 10th of November 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "MR. HOGAN: Thank you. "Can you please assume the position how you were positioned on that day? "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "MR. HOGAN: Thank you. "And finally, can you please point to the location, rather, the direction from which you believe the shot came from that wounded you on that day. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "MR. HOGAN: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, now I would like to clarify some points. You indicated the right side. Just let me put the question to you. I don't want to confuse you. I just want to clarify. You indicated a direction to the right, although you always said you had been hit on the left-hand side. So my question is: Regardless of what's left and what's right, did you indicate the direction of Spicaste Stijena in this video or the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I knew at the time I had made a mistake. I indicated with my right hand. I should have indicated with my left. I was confused at the time but, I corrected that afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It doesn't matter what hand you used but the direction you indicated. It depends on how you turn. But the direction you indicated, is that the direction of Spicaste Stijena, or is it the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, the direction was to the left. I should have indicated Spicaste Stijena to the left, but I made a mistake and I pointed to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So may I conclude that you were pointing in a direction which is not the direction where Spicaste Stijena are located?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I know it came from the side of the Spicaste Stijena, and I should have indicated that side but I indicated the opposite side. I had made a mistake, and I corrected it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do I conclude correctly that when you indicated where you had been hit from on this video, you were not pointing in the direction of Spicaste Stijena.

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, but I was mistaken. I saw that I was mistaken and I corrected my mistake. I was confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, do you sometimes, when you're talking to friends, for example, chatting, do you sometimes mistake right and left?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, one can always make a mistake. As one ages, anything can happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what do you want to do with that video clip that you played?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video is already in evidence. It's P111. I just wanted it shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me correct myself. It's Exhibit 114, at 42 minutes, 18 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Ma'am, before the Prosecutor asks you, can you clarify something for me? You've just said that you made a mistake by pointing to the right; you should have pointed to the left. Then if you point to the left -- just wait for my question. If you then point to the left, then the bullet should have hit you on the inside of your knee, not on the outside of the knee, as you showed us on the video. Are you able to explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me tell you, that's how it was. It hit me on the inside and exited on the outside. I really lost track of everything when it happened. I don't even know how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Cannata?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, with your leave, Your Honours, I have a few questions to ask. Actually, on this note, can I take the witness to page 1593 of the transcripts, which is P112.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And I quote from line 3, as a question from the Prosecution counsel, Mr. Doherty. The question goes: "Also you indicate on the video that the bullet entered your knee on the outside, and in your statement you said it entered your knee on the inside. Are you aware of that discrepancy also?" The witness answered: "I know that I started walking and that it was the inner side." Witness, Madam Witness, do you confirm that that's your answer and that that's what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: That happened, but what do I know? I was scared. When the bullet hit me, I no longer had my wits about me. You know how these moments are.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a few more questions on a different topic. Madam Witness, what did you do as an assistant cook? What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I peeled potatoes, I prepared rice, I washed dishes, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Were you engaged in any combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Did you carry any weapons on account of your work?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No. What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Were you wearing any uniform?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Were you wearing any -- wearing any uniform inside the building you were performing your duties as an assistant cook?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Were you wearing a uniform or -- were you wearing a uniform the day you were shot?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons with you the day you were shot?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. How long have you been living in Sedrenik, roughly?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I cannot tell you precisely whether it was a year or less than a year. I didn't keep track because I didn't know somebody would ask me one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: But even after the incident, you kept going to Sedrenik, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have family there. I went there to visit, and I still go there regularly to Sedrenik. That's where my family is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can I read something to you, which is adjudicated fact number 122, which was admitted by this Honourable Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Adjudicated fact from which case?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: From this case. It's one of the facts in Annex A to the Prosecution's motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts in respect of Sarajevo, which was filed on the 6th of February, 2007, and a decision was delivered in this case on the 26th of June, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just didn't understand what the purpose of this was. Did the Prosecutor want to indicate a reference with this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, he was trying to answer the question from the Bench, "adjudicated facts from which previous case," and then he referred to "adjudicated facts with respect to Sarajevo." What I wanted to find out is which case was -- in which case were those facts adjudicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: The Galic case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Galic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Galic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, I'll read a sentence to you: "Civilians in the area of Sedrenik experienced indiscriminate or direct small-arms fire originating from Spicaste Stijena, SRK-controlled territory, between September 1992 and August 1994." Would you agree with this sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think this is leading question anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am, don't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that it was dangerous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am, before you answer. There's an objection, Mr. Cannata, that you are asking a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact, it's not. This is adjudicated fact 122. It's part of the trial record. I'm putting to the witness this sentence. I will ask her to make comments on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My only question to you would be: How does it arise from cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: My understanding of the cross-examination main line was that it's being contested that the shooting at civilians which the area of Sedrenik experienced throughout the war was part of an exchange of fire, while the Prosecution's submission is that it originated from a sniper position, Spicaste Stijena, held by the SRK throughout the whole siege, that is, from September 1992 to -- as far as the adjudicated fact is concerned, August 1994. What I would like the witness to tell us is whether this pattern of fire against civilians originating from Spicaste Stijena carried out throughout November 1995, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, sorry, ma'am. Just before -- but the time range that you put in your question - let me just hold it before it disappears - had nothing to do with November 1994, sir. You said "August 1994." You didn't say "November." I beg your pardon. I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But be that as it may, I still don't see how the adjudicated fact from the Galic case with respect to September 1992 to August 1994 arises from cross-examination. The testimony of this witness is that she was injured on the 10th of December, which is outside that period that you are asking here about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. May I rephrase the question, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Madam Witness, are you aware of civilians being --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Hold on one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Madam Witness, are you aware of any sniping incident that occurred in Sedrenik from the day you were shot onwards, from the 10th of December, 1994, onwards? Were you aware of any such incident?

utterances.speaker: DERVISA SELMANOVIC
utterances.text: It happened every day. Somebody was hurt every day. Somebody was wounded, hit by a bullet, every day. I can't know after all this time, I can't remember all of that. It happened every day. They shot every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Who are "they"? Who are the people shooting from Spicaste Stijena?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that from my cross-examination and the entire testimony of this witness, the answers regarding Spicaste Stijena are very clear. I believe the Prosecutor is now going beyond the 92 statement and is trying to get some different answers from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to clarify for the record, in a clear way, what the witness has previously testified about on the first statement, paragraph 3, last line, which I quote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what the witness has previously testified about, the Trial Chamber is perfectly in a position to see when it reads that portion, when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Then I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cannata. Any questions? Any questions, Judge? Thank you very much, Mrs. Selmanovic, for coming to testify in this case. This brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. You are now excused. You may stand down. And please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware of the time. The Prosecution had hoped to have its next witness originally scheduled to begin tomorrow morning ready to continue on today, Monday; however, the witness's plane was late yesterday arriving into the Netherlands, so the witness was not able to review her materials until -- literally, it's ongoing right now. So we do not have another witness to present today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the day, okay. Thank you very much. In that event, then, we'll stand adjourned to tomorrow, at 9.00 in the morning, in Courtroom III. That's what my schedule says. Unless somebody has got a more updated schedule. Courtroom III?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I looked at the court calendar this morning, and I believe it said Courtroom II, Your Honour, but I could ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am instructed then that I am mistaken, that it will then be Courtroom II. We'll meet in here at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.08 p.m.,
